transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-14
Time: 11:00 AM EDT / 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Luis Ortega (Redwood SE); Priya Patel (Crestline); Mark Rivers (Crestline); Angela Yu (Crestline procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in, discuss capacity upgrade for Dedicated cluster, add eu-west region, and outline contract extension for 12 months with committed capacity. Plan benchmarks and security doc handoff.

Topics:
- Current usage and expected growth (QPS, token volumes)
- Dedicated capacity sizing and autoscale options
- Additional regions (eu-west) and data residency
- Contract extension timing and commercial terms
- Security/compliance artifacts (SOC 2, ISO, network diagrams)

Transcript:
[00:00] Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call, and then we'll jump in.
[00:07] Speaker 2 (Priya): Hi Maya, Priya here. Mark and Angela also on.
[00:10] Speaker 3 (Mark): Yep hi.
[00:12] Speaker 1 (Maya): Great. So high level, wanted to check where Crestline is on the renewal and expansion conversation — commit, regions, that sort of thing. We've got Luis from infra to go through sizing and bench.
[00:24] Speaker 4 (Luis): Hey all. I'll start with the usage numbers we saw last quarter, and then propose a Dedicated pool config.
[00:29] Speaker 2 (Priya): Sounds good. Just to set context: our current hosted plan is at about 18M tokens/month, peak 250 qps for the chat endpoint. We anticipate 2.5x growth after the new features roll out in June.
[00:42] Speaker 4 (Luis): Okay that maps. Our recommendation to hit your SLOs is a two-tier Dedicated pool: baseline capacity for steady state and burst nodes for peak traffic. For baseline we'd suggest 8 x A100-equivalent, plus 4 for burst. That gives room for prefix cache and batching without hitting tail latency.
[01:03] Speaker 2 (Priya): Can you clarify the autoscale behaviour — is it based on queue depth or latency? We want predictability since procurement needs committed spend numbers.
[01:14] Speaker 4 (Luis): Autoscale can be configured by target p99 latency or by request queue length. For committed plan we can reserve baseline and then allow controlled burst with a cap. The pricing difference between reserve and burst is in the quote — Maya will follow up.
[01:30] Speaker 1 (Maya): Right, I'll include the pricing tiers in the sheet. Another ask from legal/procurement was regional isolation — Crestline wants eu data residency for EU customers, can we spin up an eu-west Dedicated cluster?
[01:44] Speaker 3 (Mark): Yes EU residency is a hard req for some products.
[01:47] Speaker 1 (Maya): We can. Redwood Dedicated supports region pinning and isolated control plane in the private deployment. For hosted accounts we can allocate capacity in eu-west and ensure logs and KV cache don't leave region. Note — some of the network detail is in the SOC/ISO pack.
[02:06] Speaker 2 (Priya): How quick is spin up for a new region? We have a launch window mid-June.
[02:12] Speaker 4 (Luis): Typical provisioning for a Dedicated pool in a new region is 2–4 weeks assuming capacity availability. If you want guaranteed spin-up we recommend a soft commit so we can pre-book nodes. Also if you want on-prem we'll need longer lead times.
[02:29] Speaker 1 (Maya): There's also an order-of-ops question — do you want a 12-month committed extension with the extra region included, or do you want a short term renewal and add region after the June launch?
[02:40] Speaker 2 (Priya): Prefer a single contract if the economics work. Procurement wants predictability. Angela, thoughts?
[02:45] Speaker 5 (Angela): From procurement side, a 12-month committed capacity with clearly defined baseline is easiest, but we need a clear exit/fallback clause and SLA credits. Also pricing details for burst.
[02:57] Speaker 1 (Maya): Totally. We'll draft extension terms with baseline capacity, burst caps, and SLA language. I'll add termination and fallback to hosted models as options.
[03:08] Speaker 4 (Luis): On the technical side, we should run an end-to-end benchmark: run chat-gen and embeddings at your expected QPS across us-east and eu-west, measure p50/p95/p99, memory/KV behavior. I can drive that if we get access to a staging key and a small data subset.
[03:25] Speaker 2 (Priya): We'll provide a staging account and sample payloads. Also we need to ensure KMS integration for key management — we use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS for some services.
[03:36] Speaker 4 (Luis): Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and KMS integration for Dedicated via customer KMS in the region. There was a minor hiccup earlier with the K V cache naming in the docs — sometimes it shows 'KV cash' in the auto doc, sorry transcriber — but functionally it's supported.
[03:52] Speaker 1 (Maya): No worries. We'll include the KMS runbook in the security pack. On SOC 2 / ISO docs, I'll attach the latest report and network diagram after the call.
[04:01] Speaker 2 (Priya): Great. One question — any competitor mentions from the team? We've been talking to CloudAI and they offer cheaper spot pricing but without regional isolation.
[04:12] Speaker 1 (Maya): Noted. We also saw some interest in Anthropic offerings for hallucination controls, but your workloads are throughput-first so our Dedicated offering is a closer fit.
[04:22] Speaker 5 (Angela): From procurement, can you provide the pricing delta for adding eu-west? Need it for the internal approval.
[04:29] Speaker 1 (Maya): I'll send a revised quote with region add-on line items.
[04:33] Speaker 4 (Luis): Another ops note: when we do the benchmark we'll exercise prefix caching and batch sizes, and show cost/latency tradeoffs. There's usually a sweet spot for batch size that lowers token cost without pushing p99 over your SLO.
[04:48] Speaker 2 (Priya): Can Luis include sample configs? We'll need them for our infra team to mirror.
[04:53] Speaker 4 (Luis): Yep will share a runbook and sample yaml for autoscale policies and kernel selection notes.
[04:59] Speaker 1 (Maya): Recap — Maya sends revised pricing and SOC/ISO + network diagram by 4/16; Luis runs benchmark plan and gives runbook by 4/21; Priya sends infra diagram and QPS numbers by 4/18. We'll aim to have a draft contract extension the following week.
[05:13] Speaker 2 (Priya): That works. Anything else?
[05:16] Speaker 5 (Angela): Please include SLA credits and an explicit fallback to hosted model in the draft.
[05:21] Speaker 1 (Maya): Will do. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up via email with links to the docs.
[05:27] Speaker 3 (Mark): Thanks.
[05:30] Speaker 2 (Priya): Bye.

References / shared artifacts: "Redwood Dedicated pricing sheet" (link in follow-up), "SOC2-ISO-pack.pdf" (will be shared), benchmark runbook (Luis will share).

End of transcript.
